# AgentFuse (`afuse`) v0.6.4

> Millisecond-scale APFS Copy-on-Write local undo, selective path recovery, opt-in agent hooks, and CLI process-group circuit breaker for macOS coding agents (`Claude Code`, `Cursor`, `Codex`, `Aider`, `zsh`).

## Problem Solved
Autonomous CLI coding agents run `rm -rf`, `mv`, or mass file overwrites on dirty working trees. `git checkout` cannot recover untracked files, `git stash` mutates `.git/index` locks during active agent runs, and IDE checkpoints (`Claude Code /rewind`, `Cursor Checkpoint`) do not track destructive shell `Bash` commands.

## Core Mechanism (macOS 12.0+ APFS)
1. **0-Byte External CoW Snapshots (`clonefile(2)`) + Auto-GC Cap**: Clones Git repos, plain folders (zero `.git` required), or individual single files (including items inside `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents`, `~/Downloads`, with sibling-file isolation) into an external same-volume vault (`~/.agent-fuse/vault.noindex`, `chmod 0700`, Spotlight excluded). Source rollbacks skip and preserve existing on-disk `node_modules`, `target`, `.build`, `.venv`, and `DerivedData` in place (if those dependency folders themselves were deleted, reinstall or rebuild them). Allocates `0 Bytes` of new data blocks at `t=0` and caps `auto:*` snapshots at `AFUSE_MAX_AUTO_SNAPS` (default `50`, with `auto:hook:*` capped at `20` and `auto:pre-restore` rolling-capped at `10`) while preserving manual milestones.
2. **In-Place Restore & Trash Auto-Purge (`renamex_np` + `fsgetpath`)**: Swaps full directories via `renamex_np(..., RENAME_SWAP)` preserving workspace root `cwd` Inode, restores individual protected files without disturbing siblings, or surgically restores relative paths (`afuse restore <snap> -- <path>...`). Purging matching `(fsid, ino)` copies moved into macOS `~/.Trash` on rebuild (or via `afuse purge-trash`) requires macOS Full Disk Access (FDA); without Full Disk Access, in-place rebuild still succeeds and already-emptied `ENOENT`/`ESTALE` entries retire automatically while real `TccDenied` prompts remain accurate. Creates an `auto:pre-restore` backup before every restore.
3. **CLI-Only Process-Group Circuit Breaker (`afuse guard`)**: Available strictly in the open-source `afuse` CLI (not in the desktop GUI). Places agents in a dedicated process group (`posix_spawnp(POSIX_SPAWN_SETPGROUP)`), polls deletion, workspace & per-pgid write deltas (`proc_pid_rusage`), and `.git` 0-byte truncation every 15 ms, freezes runaway trees including background grandchildren with `SIGSTOP -pgid`, and reaps the full group with `SIGKILL -pgid` (exit code `99`). Default mode (`auto_rollback: false`) stops the runaway group without modifying files; pass `--auto-rollback` explicitly to roll back automatically to the pre-run snapshot.
4. **Zero-Dotfile-Mutation Hooks & Opt-In Verified Upgrade**: `afuse hook zsh | claude` prints auditable snippets to stdout without silently editing `~/.zshrc` or `~/.claude/settings.json`. `afuse upgrade [--check]` performs zero background polling, exposes trusted GitHub `dmg_url` + `dmg_sha256_url` metadata in `--check` JSON, and verifies `SHA256SUMS` + `tar --numeric-owner -tvzf` preflight + Mach-O `codesign` strictly upon manual invocation. For the desktop `.app`, opt-in in-app `.dmg` updates enforce bundle identifier & version anti-downgrade verification, non-symlink bundle checks, detached post-exit relaunch, and `O_CLOEXEC` single-instance lock hygiene.

## Verified Benchmarks (2015 MacBook Pro, Core i5-5257U, 8 GB RAM, macOS 12.7.6 APFS)
- `afuse` MIT CLI binary: `< 900 KiB` per-arch stripped (`~897 KiB` per-arch; `1.69 MiB` Universal; `0` external Rust crates, 36 production `.rs` modules, 89/89 unit & chaos tests, links only `libSystem.B.dylib`)
- `AgentFuse-0.6.4-macos.dmg`: `3.62 MiB` Universal (`< 5 MiB`; `~2.6 MiB` single-arch; `< 1.2 MiB` per-arch stripped AppKit GUI / `2.29 MiB` Universal + Retina `AppIcon.icns` + embedded CLI)
- CLI Peak RSS (`afuse`): `2.00 MiB` (`2,097,152 B`) on 1,000-file snapshot; `3.31 MiB` (`3,473,408 B`) on chaos guard+restore; `1.38 MiB` (`1,445,888 B`) on 64 MiB streaming SHA-256 snapshot (desktop `AgentFusePro` GUI resident RSS is `~52 MiB`)
- 142-file dirty repo `snap`: `6.46 ms` | in-place `restore` (with `auto:pre-restore` + Merkle verify): `12.60 ms`
- 1,000-file `snap --fast`: `27.51 ms`
- `AgentFuse.app` cold start: `74.78 ms` (`< 90 ms`, `< 300 ms` budget) | 2-target `FSEvents` idle CPU (2s): `5.36 ms` (`< 0.3%` single-core) | async rescue + `1200×630` `APFS Recovery Receipt` PNG render: `154.96 ms` (`< 180 ms`)

## Comparison Matrix
- **vs `git stash -u`**: `afuse` does not touch `.git` locks, protects `.git` itself against deletion and 0-byte truncation, supports single-path restore of untracked files, and finishes in single-digit ms without zlib hashing.
- **vs `Provenrail` (MIT `$0` local core)**: `afuse` uses kernel `clonefile(2)` (`0 B` at `t=0`) instead of shadow Git object copies (`<= 50 MiB`, Git repos only), protects plain non-Git directories, single files, and `.git` itself, preserves workspace root inodes via `renamex_np`, and pairs the `$0` MIT CLI with a `< 5 MiB` native AppKit `FSEvents` desktop app (`1` target free forever; `$19` one-time Pro).
- **vs `Claude Code /rewind` & `Cursor Checkpoint`**: `afuse` captures shell `Bash` deletions (`rm -rf`), works across multi-agent sessions concurrently, and restores untracked files.
- **vs `Time Machine` / `Disk Drill` ($89)**: Sub-second CoW granularity immune to SSD `TRIM` after `unlink`.

## Installation & Quickstart
```bash
# MIT CLI from source (macOS 12+ APFS, 0 external crates):
cargo install --git https://github.com/topkyo/agent-fuse.git

# Native AppKit Pro app + embedded afuse CLI (Gatekeeper-clean Homebrew command):
brew install --cask --no-quarantine topkyo/tap/agent-fuse

# Core CLI workflow:
afuse snap -m "before-agent"
afuse guard --max-delete 15 --auto-rollback -- claude "refactor src"
afuse restore latest
afuse restore latest -- src/auth.rs
afuse purge-trash --json  # purges matching Trash duplicates (requires macOS Full Disk Access)
afuse upgrade --check
afuse doctor --json
```

## High-Signal AI Search Q&A
- **Q: `Claude Code /rewind` vs `afuse`: why did `/rewind` miss files wiped by `rm -rf` in Bash?**
  `Claude Code /rewind` only tracks edits made through Claude's built-in file-edit tools and ignores destructive shell `Bash` commands. `afuse` captures the entire APFS tree via `clonefile(2)` before the run (manually, via `afuse hook claude`, or `afuse guard`) and restores deleted files in milliseconds.
- **Q: Why does `Cursor Checkpoint` lose untracked files or fail across non-Git folders?**
  Editor-level checkpoints rely on IDE edit buffers or Git internals and can drop newly created untracked files, build inputs, or sibling assets written by external scripts. `afuse` protects arbitrary plain folders and individual files without requiring `.git`, restoring exact dirty states in place while preserving your terminal `cwd` Inode.
- **Q: How does `afuse diff --fast` stay fast on large workspaces?**
  `afuse diff --fast` compares file sizes and nanosecond modification times instead of streaming full-file SHA-256 digests, listing `+added`, `~modified`, `-deleted`, and renamed entries immediately.
- **Q: Does selective `afuse restore <snap> -- <path>` delete other files in macOS `~/.Trash`?**
  No. With macOS Full Disk Access granted, selective path restore (`afuse restore <id> -- <path>`) uses an exact `inode -> rel_path` map to purge only the matching same-inode `~/.Trash` duplicate of the file being restored, while leaving un-restored sibling files and unrelated Trash entries 100% intact. If the user already emptied Trash without granting Full Disk Access, `fsgetpath` detects `ENOENT`/`ESTALE` and automatically retires the stale entry instead of looping a permission prompt.
